title: Flat scalar extension and conjugation on a smooth group congruence module
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $J\subseteq A$ an ideal with $J^2=0$, and $G\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a smooth affine group scheme of finite presentation [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Its identity, multiplication and inverse satisfy the diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] over $\operatorname{Spec}A$. For an $A$-algebra $B$ put $K_B=\ker(G(B)\to G(B/JB))$. Give $K_B$ its $B/JB$-module structure from [lem-sfb-group-space-square-zero-kernel-module], with multiplication of points as addition; regard it also as a $B$-module annihilated by $JB$. Set $M=K_A$. Here flatness of $B$ means that $-\otimes_A B$ preserves exact sequences of $A$-modules, and tensor products have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For every flat commutative $A$-algebra $B$, the map
$$E_B:M\otimes_A B\longrightarrow K_B,\qquad m\otimes b\longmapsto b\cdot(m\text{ extended to }B)$$
is an isomorphism of $B$-modules. It is natural for every $A$-algebra homomorphism $B\to B'$ between flat $A$-algebras, including homomorphisms that are not flat: under $E_B,E_{B'}$ the map on points is $m\otimes b\mapsto m\otimes b'$, where $b'$ is the image of $b$. At $B=A$ this identifies $m\otimes1$ with $m$. For every commutative $A$-algebra $B$ and every $g\in G(B)$, conjugation $k\mapsto gkg^{-1}$ on $K_B$ is a $B$-linear automorphism, natural for homomorphisms of $A$-algebras. No field or noetherian hypothesis, and no finite-generation hypothesis on $J$, is imposed.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/luminysga3smf.pdf . Proof of Corollary B.2.6, printed p.287, identification of the congruence kernel with the quasi-coherent Lie module and identification of conjugation with the adjoint action. Agent explicit flat-scalar-extension formulation of that identification.

proof.text: Write $G=\operatorname{Spec}C$, and let $\epsilon:C\to A$ be the identity point, using [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. By [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], $C$ is a finitely presented $A$-algebra. Thus [lem-sfb-ring-finite-presentation-differentials] gives a finite presentation $C^u\to C^v\to\Omega_{C/A}\to0$. Set $P=\Omega_{C/A}\otimes_{C,\epsilon}A$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] to that presentation gives $A^u\to A^v\to P\to0$, so $P$ is finitely presented over $A$. The identifications $C^v\otimes_C A=A^v$ send each basis tensor $e_i\otimes a$ to $ae_i$; they require no flatness.

source.place: Tag 00RY, lemma-differentials-finitely-presented; Tag 00DF, lemma-tensor-product-exact. The affine finite-presentation input is Morphisms Tag 01TQ.

proof.text:
For any $A$-algebra $B$, write $I=JB$ and $\epsilon_B:C\to A\to B$. Products of generators $jb$ of $I$ vanish in pairs, hence $I^2=0$. The canonical module identification in [lem-sfb-group-space-square-zero-kernel-module] and the difference formula in [lem-sfb-space-square-zero-lift-linearization] have the following explicit affine form:
$$\chi_B:K_B\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,I),\qquad \chi_B(k)(dc\otimes a)=a\bigl(k^\sharp(c)-\epsilon_B(c)\bigr).$$
Here the target is a $B$-module by multiplication in $I$. Indeed $D=k^\sharp-\epsilon_B$ is additive, vanishes on $A$, and satisfies $D(cc')=\epsilon_B(c)D(c')+\epsilon_B(c')D(c)$ because $D(c)D(c')=0$. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], followed by the tensor universal property in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], identifies such $D$ with the displayed $A$-linear maps. Conversely $h:P\to I$ gives the algebra map $c\mapsto\epsilon_B(c)+h(dc\otimes1)$: its multiplicativity is precisely the same expansion with the quadratic term zero. These constructions are inverse. This is the cited sheaf difference derivation on affine coordinates; equality of its formulas on $dc$ identifies its scalar operations with those of the module structure specified in the item. The cited kernel theorem identifies point multiplication with addition. In particular $M=K_A\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,J)$.

source.place: Tags 0618 and 04D0, lemma-difference-derivation and lemma-action-by-derivations; equation-D. Agent affine expansion of these identifications.

proof.text:
Now assume $B$ is flat. Tensor the injection $J\hookrightarrow A$ with $B$: by the exactness convention in the statement the map $J\otimes_A B\to A\otimes_A B=B$ is injective, and its image is exactly the ideal $JB$ (its pure tensors have images $jb$, which generate that ideal). Thus
$$\lambda_B:J\otimes_A B\xrightarrow{\sim}JB,\qquad j\otimes b\mapsto jb.$$
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-hom-finitely-presented] with source module $P$, target module $J$, and ring map $A\to B$. Its hypotheses hold by step 1 and the assumed flatness. After swapping tensor factors it gives an isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,J)\otimes_A B\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_B(P\otimes_A B,J\otimes_A B).$$
Compose with $\lambda_B$ and the tensor adjunction $\operatorname{Hom}_B(P\otimes_A B,JB)=\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,JB)$. Explicitly this last adjunction sends $f$ to $p\mapsto f(p\otimes1)$, with inverse $h\mapsto(p\otimes b\mapsto bh(p))$. The resulting isomorphism is $h\otimes b\mapsto(p\mapsto b\,h(p))$.

source.place: Tag 087R, lemma-pseudo-coherence-and-base-change-ext (1). The image calculation uses the stated definition of flatness.

proof.text:
Under $\chi_A$ and $\chi_B$ the isomorphism of step 3 is exactly $E_B$. To verify this and all the asserted naturality, let $\varphi:B\to B'$ be any $A$-algebra map. It takes $JB$ into $JB'$ and satisfies
$$\chi_{B'}(k_{B'})(dc\otimes1)=\varphi(k^\sharp(c)-\epsilon_B(c))=\varphi(\chi_B(k)(dc\otimes1)).$$
The same holds for every $p\in P$ by additivity and $A$-linearity. Consequently the point map is $\varphi$-semilinear in these module coordinates, with no flatness assumption on $\varphi$. In particular extension of $m\in M$ corresponds to $p\mapsto\chi_A(m)(p)$ viewed in $JB$. Thus $b$ times that point corresponds to $p\mapsto b\chi_A(m)(p)$, proving the formula for $E_B$ and its balancedness. For flat $B,B'$ the two composites on $m\otimes b$ both give the point with coordinates $p\mapsto\varphi(b)\chi_A(m)(p)$; the tensor generators of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] give equality everywhere. At $B=A$, $\chi_A(E_A(m\otimes1))=\chi_A(m)$, so injectivity gives the required normalization.

source.place: Tag 0618, lemma-difference-derivation: explicit coefficient-map calculation using the difference derivations of step 2.

proof.text: Finally fix any $B$ and $g\in G(B)$. Work with the $B$-group $G_B$, whose $B$-points are canonically $G(B)$. Its conjugation map $u=\operatorname{Int}(g)$ is a morphism over $\operatorname{Spec}B$, fixes the identity, and has inverse $\operatorname{Int}(g^{-1})$, by the multiplication and inverse diagrams in the hypothesis. Apply [lem-sfb-space-square-zero-lift-linearization] with base $S=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $X=Y=G_B$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $T_0=\operatorname{Spec}(B/JB)$ and $a$ the identity section. It says that $k\mapsto gkg^{-1}=u\circ k$ acts on difference derivations by the $B/JB$-linear map $D\mapsto D\circ u^\sharp$. The module identification of [lem-sfb-group-space-square-zero-kernel-module] is the same one as for $G$ on these test schemes: a map into $G_B$ is the pair of its map into $G$ and its fixed structure map into $\operatorname{Spec}B$, so its difference derivation is the one in step 2. Hence conjugation is $B/JB$-linear and therefore $B$-linear on $K_B$. Applying the inverse conjugation proves invertibility. For any $\varphi:B\to B'$, functoriality of multiplication and inverse gives $(gkg^{-1})_{B'}=g_{B'}k_{B'}g_{B'}^{-1}$, proving naturality, also when $B$ or $B'$ is not flat.

source.place: Tag 04D0, lemma-action-by-derivations; functorial difference formula. This realizes the linear conjugation assertion in Conrad, Corollary B.2.6, proof, printed p.287.

Its only citer, lem-sfb-split-torus-infinitesimal-conjugacy, uses it exactly as stated: Laurent algebras are free, M tensor C_d, naturality under substitution, linear conjugation. Step 1: the Mathlib leaves 01TQ, 00RY and 00DF give that C is finitely presented over A, Omega_{C/A} is finitely presented, and so is P = e^*Omega. Step 2: the step proves the bijection between the kernel K_B and A-derivations C->JB itself. The group law and scalars come from the linearization lemma's formula delta(k) = k^sharp - e^sharp. Since both delta and chi_B are bijections, the global-sections map between them is linear and bijective. The kernel-module statement only says 'canonical'; its proof step 1 shows that this is the linearization lemma's delta at the identity. I accept this and it is not a new fault. Step 3: the item's own flatness convention implies def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, so lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-hom-finitely-presented (087R) applies with M=P and N=J, with no finiteness of J needed. I checked the composite through J tensor B = JB and the tensor-Hom adjunction. Step 4 is elementary as marked: naturality is semilinear in coordinates, and E_B and the normalization at B=A are as stated. Step 5: I checked the linearization lemma with S=T=Spec B, X=Y=G_B, T_0=Spec(B/JB) and u=Int(g); identifying G_B over Spec B with G over Spec A is restriction of derivations from C tensor B to C. That is no step of the trace formula or of Poincare duality, and the base stmt_dep kernel-module lemma already reaches it, so it is outside the assumed statements.
